title: Animal tissues organs and organ systems
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for AQA GCSE Biology (8461) (status of the source: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms and clues: 4.2.2-c25 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.2.2-c14 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.2.2-c27 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.2.2-c26 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition. Questions: 4.2.2-q11, 4.2.2-q15, 4.2.2-q16, 4.2.2-q12, 4.2.2-q17, 4.2.2-q13, 4.2.2-q18, 4.2.2-q14.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Red blood cell
items.clue: A blood cell that carries oxygen.

items.label: Heart
items.clue: An organ that pumps blood around the body.

items.label: Platelet
items.clue: A small fragment of cell suspended in the plasma that helps the blood to clot at a wound.

items.label: White blood cell
items.clue: A blood cell that defends the body against pathogens, for example by engulfing them or by producing antibodies.

questions.stem: Which statement about the double circulatory system is correct?

options.text: Blood passes through the heart once each circuit.
Arteries carry blood with oxygen to the lungs.
The right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs.
The left ventricle pumps blood to the lungs.

questions.explanation: The right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs where gas exchange takes place, while the left ventricle pumps blood around the rest of the body.

questions.stem: A photograph shows the cells in a sample of blood. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Platelets move around the blood and destroy pathogens.
Plasma is the liquid that carries oxygen to the cells.
Red blood cells have a nucleus that controls oxygen use.
Red blood cells have no nucleus, so they carry more oxygen.

questions.explanation: A red blood cell is adapted to its function of carrying oxygen: it has no nucleus, leaving more room for haemoglobin.

questions.stem: Which statement about the treatment of coronary heart disease is correct?

options.text: Statins are used to widen the blocked coronary arteries.
Stents are used to keep the coronary arteries open.
Stents are used to lower the level of blood cholesterol.
Artificial hearts are used to cure the heart disease.

questions.explanation: In coronary heart disease fatty material narrows the coronary arteries, and stents are used to keep them open.

questions.stem: Which feature of the alveoli increases the rate of gaseous exchange?

options.text: A wide tube that carries air down to the lungs.
A thick outer wall that resists air pressure.
A supply of plasma that takes up the oxygen.
A large surface area and a good blood supply.

questions.explanation: The alveoli are adapted for gaseous exchange by a large surface area and the capillary network that surrounds them.

questions.stem: A person has a heart valve that has developed a leak. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Blood flows backwards through the leaking valve.
The volume of blood pumped stays the same.
Only a heart transplant can treat the problem.
An artificial heart gives a permanent cure.

questions.explanation: A faulty valve that leaks lets blood flow backwards, so less blood is pumped forward to the body.

questions.stem: Which pairing of a blood vessel with its structure is correct?

options.text: Artery: thick wall resists the high pressure.
Vein: thick muscular wall resists high pressure.
Capillary: thick wall resists the blood pressure.
Artery: valves stop blood flowing backwards.

questions.explanation: An artery carries blood away from the heart at high pressure, so its wall is thick, with muscle and elastic fibres.

questions.stem: Why might an artificial heart be used for a patient with heart failure?

options.text: It keeps a patient alive while awaiting a donor.
It replaces a faulty valve inside the patient.
It cures the heart failure without any further care.
It lowers the level of cholesterol in the blood.

questions.explanation: Artificial hearts are occasionally used to keep patients alive whilst waiting for a heart transplant, or to allow the heart to rest as an aid to recovery.

questions.stem: A heart pumps 300 cm3 of blood in 4 seconds. What is the rate of blood flow?

options.text: 1200 cm3 per second
75 cm3 per second
300 cm3 per second
0.01 cm3 per second

questions.explanation: Rate of blood flow is the volume divided by the time taken: 300 cm3 divided by 4 seconds.
